description: End-to-end shop order saga: user registration → graph-based product recommendations → cart operations → order placement → multi-step saga orchestration with compensation
loopback_caveat: Results are not equivalent to network-path benchmarks. transport_mode=loopback-h2c is mandatory in all result artifacts.

concurrency.note: 100 VUs with 800-2500ms think-time between saga steps

neo4j.equivalence_note: Saga orchestration via platform-recommended approach: exeris=flow-native, quarkus=axon-framework, spring=axon-framework. Not algorithmically equivalent. Comparison reflects real-world platform adoption cost, not isolated runtime performance.

pgq_pure.equivalence_note: Saga orchestration via platform-recommended approach: exeris=flow-native, quarkus=axon-framework, spring=axon-framework. Not algorithmically equivalent. Comparison reflects real-world platform adoption cost, not isolated runtime performance.

age_compat.equivalence_note: Saga orchestration via platform-recommended approach: exeris=flow-native, quarkus=axon-framework, spring=axon-framework. Not algorithmically equivalent. Comparison reflects real-world platform adoption cost, not isolated runtime performance.

pgq.notes: Use pgq_pure or age_compat; do not aggregate alias with new tracks

seed.idempotency_guarantee: Re-running seed.sql produces identical state across users, products, inventory, product_relationships, and user_purchase_history tables. Results without passing pre-run verification are invalid.

workload_invariants.payment_fail_rate_note: All targets participating in cross-runtime comparison MUST be configured with identical payment_fail_rate. Runs where any target deviates from this value are invalid for comparative purposes. Exeris: configured via EXERIS_SAGA_PAYMENT_FAIL_RATE env var. Quarkus/Spring Axon targets: must configure equivalent fail injection via their own mechanism at the same rate.

k6_poll_budget.rationale: 25-attempt budget allows compensation (COMPENSATING state) time to reach terminal COMPENSATED state before marking saga as unresolved

quarkus_axon_neo4j_v1.claim_scope_note: Axon saga targets record end-to-end HTTP latency under the Axon Framework event-sourcing execution model. Request-path DB writes differ structurally from Exeris community (Axon: in-process command dispatch + in-memory SimpleEventBus event publish — no synchronous DB writes in HTTP request path; Exeris: INSERT orders + INSERT order_items + UPDATE saga_id — 3 synchronous DB writes in HTTP request path). Inventory reservation, multi-step saga state transitions, and compensation are not executed in the request path under Axon. Status poll served from in-memory projection (ConcurrentHashMap), not from a DB read. Cross-target latency comparison with exeris-community-app is NOT supported at this claim scope.
quarkus_axon_neo4j_v1.workload_note: product_level_including_framework: Axon Framework event-sourcing saga model vs Exeris CoreFlowEngine native saga. order_id is a logical AtomicLong saga correlation identifier, not a DB BIGSERIAL row. status_poll_comparison_excluded: true.
